### Final-package focused 202605 health validation

Validated combined head `76ff4c8376fd97515bb579160e9cebb92fa13ddb` from this PR on Arista 720DT m0 running `SONiC.20260510.20`, without changing product source or the published head.

Artifact identity: package SHA-256 `5a284b693cd85d7c4a3c5869dfba7b7a36e54a3b6909ad2ebb20f94f7ef346e7`; running candidate ELF SHA-256 `260a1e253229403e1e9aa83a61a46f054f5eeddc418e0acbf887cf95bcf4e855`. These are the same final-source artifacts used for the previously published startup/Redis-loss and complete DHCP regression results.

**Counter synchronization and snapshot handoff**

- Seeded counters to 7, synchronized all four actual IPv4/IPv6 RX/TX workers, observed exactly one main-thread post-synchronization health skip, then normal health evaluation resumed.
- Cleared the seeded interface counters to zero; verified all four cache-update acknowledgments, fresh zero-valued current/snapshot debug counters, snapshot refresh after the main-thread skip, and no false disparity or unsigned-underflow marker.
- Paused without sending the completion signal; observed health evaluation skip during the active pause, the normal clear timeout, exactly one post-timeout snapshot handoff, and resumed health evaluation without a false disparity.

**First-hop DHCPv6 health semantics and real loss control**

The final focused target passed; its posttest passed all five checks.

| Scenario | Observed result |
|---|---|
| Healthy Solicit/Request to Relay-Forward and Relay-Reply to Advertise/Reply traffic | 25 completed health evaluations; 24 active forward/reply windows; 24 windows with RX activity and zero same-type TX activity, but positive relay-transformed TX activity; zero disparity alerts |
| DHCPv6 relay deliberately suspended while sending valid Solicit traffic | 25 health evaluations; 24 RX-without-forwarding windows; TX Relay-Forward remained zero; real disparity alerts began at the default 198-second threshold |
| Relay resumed and healthy traffic repeated | 7 health evaluations; 5 active forward/reply windows; zero further disparity alerts |

This demonstrates that the health fix accepts normal relay transformations without merely disabling real packet-loss detection. The existing packet exchange/verifier was reused with paced traffic so diagnostic logging remained below the normal rsyslog rate limit; no logging protection or product timeout was disabled.

Standard pretest: **11 passed, 3 expected skips**. Final focused target: **1 passed, zero failures/errors/skips**. Posttest: **5 passed**. The target uses normal health-window and alarm-threshold settings.

**Restoration**

The candidate was stopped normally and removed. Saved counter values, cache state and synchronization flags were restored. The stock binary remained unchanged and was independently verified afterward as SHA-256 `9f591f9255dfd7231d11e6b18dfc0bd03ad986e0bc152cc7300eaa14c72748cc`; Supervisor reported DHCPmon running. Redis returned PONG, systemd was running, all 12 IPv4/IPv6 BGP peers were established, and no new DHCPmon core was found.

**Scope and retained limitations**

This is focused proof of synchronization and first-hop DHCPv6 SARR health, genuine loss detection and recovery on the exact combined release package. It supplements, rather than replaces, the earlier **48 passed / 11 skipped** complete DHCP suite and **16 exercised controlled Redis-loss exits / 18 attempts**, with zero aborts/new cores:

https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcpmon/pull/121#issuecomment-6139803830

The additional nested-relay-wrapper probe did not establish its expected forwarding on this older image and remains a coverage limitation; it is not described as passing, and it has not been attributed to this PR without a stock comparison. The earlier helper failures and their corrections are retained: slow per-write CLI spawning exceeded the clear timeout; an assertion incorrectly included live management counters; legacy nested packets did not match the monitor profile; and unpaced debug traffic saturated normal rsyslog rate limiting. These are not hidden by the final passing first-hop result.

The existing `LOGGER.dhcp4relay` CONFIG_DB warning and the older-image master regression outcome remain recorded in the linked root evidence. No latest-master, Dual-ToR, or all-nested-profile qualification is claimed.

@StormLiangMS @ashutosh-agrawal Please review the current master PR. Xichen review is complete, the exact-head CI is green, and all visible review threads are resolved. We will assess the 202605 backport scope separately.

The 202605 delivery is now consolidated in one manual backport:

https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcpmon/pull/122

### Why we chose to fix this

The original `tests/process_monitoring/test_critical_process_monitoring.py::test_monitoring_critical_processes` test deliberately terminates Redis and `redis_bmp`, verifies the expected critical-process alerts, and then performs system recovery. It does not require DHCPmon or the other Redis-dependent daemons to remain operational while Redis is unavailable.

After Redis was killed, DHCPmon's periodic `db_update_callback()` attempted its normal COUNTERS_DB update and received a Redis `Broken pipe` exception. Because that exception escaped the libevent C callback boundary, C++ invoked `std::terminate()`: DHCPmon exited through SIGABRT and generated a core instead of reporting a controlled dependency failure.

The failure was reproducible but timing-sensitive in the broader test:

- The original binary produced a DHCPmon core in all 6 targeted reproductions.
- Historical 720DT internal-202605 nightly results produced the DHCPmon core in 9 of 18 otherwise-successful process-monitoring runs.

We considered same-process Redis reconnection, but chose controlled failure shutdown instead. Redis is a system-level dependency used for DHCPmon state, configuration, and counters, and the destructive test already owns whole-system recovery. The focused requirement is therefore to prevent an exception escaping a callback and turning the expected dependency failure into SIGABRT/core generation.

This PR catches `std::exception` directly at the two selected callback boundaries: the periodic DB update and packet processing callbacks. It logs the fatal exception, requests failure shutdown of the main and worker event loops, joins the workers, performs the existing cleanup, and retains a nonzero process result. It does not add Redis retry/reconnection or suppress core collection.

The earlier PR121-only release package was exercised in 12 targeted attempts across six 720DT m0 beds. Nine attempts reached the fatal callback and three were timing misses; none of the 12 produced a DHCPmon core or SIGABRT. Every bed was restored to its stock binary and finished with Redis healthy, DHCPmon running, systemd running, and all 12 BGP sessions established.

That is historical evidence for the earlier PR121 implementation. Current startup-safe validation is reported separately below.

### Combined 202605 backport

It contains:

- This controlled callback-failure shutdown change.
- The counter-synchronization snapshot protection from https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcpmon/pull/114.
- The DHCPv6 relay-aware RX/TX health correction from https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcpmon/pull/101.

The final combined release head is `76ff4c8376fd97515bb579160e9cebb92fa13ddb`, one signed commit against 202605. The only manual PR101 conflict was in `dhcp_device.h`: the resolution preserves the existing 202605 aggregate-health enum values and applies only the DHCPv6 positive-health description and behavior. No PR99/PR100 interface-observability changes were imported.

### Startup-race correction and current evidence

The race is fixed in both final publications: master `c5bc7543cd32be3c2b64cb0cc22fdf800b74e09e` and 202605 `76ff4c8376fd97515bb579160e9cebb92fa13ddb`.

Each fatal-stop path now calls `loopbreak()` followed by a queued `loopexit()` on the same base. An active loop breaks after its callback; a late-starting loop consumes the retained exit request. The originating callback's loop retains `got_exit == false`, preserving the unchanged nonzero failure classification. No readiness handshake or new failure state is needed.

Both final heads passed amd64, arm64, armhf, aggregate, DCO and EasyCLA: [master build 1246902](https://dev.azure.com/mssonic/be1b070f-be15-4154-aade-b1d3bfb17054/_build/results?buildId=1246902) and [202605 build 1246903](https://dev.azure.com/mssonic/be1b070f-be15-4154-aade-b1d3bfb17054/_build/results?buildId=1246903).

Fresh 202605 runtime proof uses SONiC.20260510.20 on Arista 720DT m0 and package SHA-256 `5a284b693cd85d7c4a3c5869dfba7b7a36e54a3b6909ad2ebb20f94f7ef346e7`. That package's build 1246898 CI merge tree exactly equals the final published release tree.

- Stock Redis/redis_bmp SIGKILL reproduced SIGABRT and a new DHCPmon core.
- A deterministic actual-binary control held the main and three later workers before dispatch, then invoked the registered production packet callback once with an invalid socket to exercise its exception handler. The pre-fix binary returned only its originating loop and hung until the watchdog killed it.
- The fixed binary returned from all five loops, completed joins/cleanup, and exited with status 1 without another exception. The originating loop reported `got_exit=0, got_break=1`; the other four reported `got_exit=1, got_break=0`.
- Normal SIGTERM shutdown logged successful termination and exited with status 0.
- Eighteen completed identical fixed-package Redis-loss attempts yielded sixteen fatal-callback/status-1 shutdowns and two timing misses, with zero DHCPmon aborts and zero new DHCPmon cores.

The startup fixture is validation-only; it is not a production-code change or a real Dual-ToR packet/Redis reproduction.

### Final 202605 DHCP regression

The complete seven-module `tests/dhcp_relay` suite finished on the final-source package: **48 passed, 11 skipped, zero test failures or errors**. Standard pretest passed (11 passed, 3 skipped), and posttest passed (5 passed).

The candidate binary hash was checked after the suite. No new DHCPmon core was found. The original stock binary was restored byte-for-byte (SHA-256 `9f591f9255dfd7231d11e6b18dfc0bd03ad986e0bc152cc7300eaa14c72748cc`), and final checks verified DHCPmon running, Redis PONG, systemd running, and all 12 BGP sessions established.

The test framework recorded a CONFIG_DB metadata warning for creation of the default `LOGGER.dhcp4relay` entry when exercising the SONiC relay agent. That warning was retained, not suppressed. Consequently, the passing test/health results must not be described as wholly unchanged configuration metadata.

The automatically started same-package run on another 720DT m0 bed also finished with 48 passed, 11 skipped, zero test failures/errors, posttest 5 passed, no new DHCPmon core, verified stock restoration, and 12/12 BGP. It is supporting evidence, not an additional required campaign.

### Master regression outcome

Master original-failure, actual-binary startup control/fix and normal shutdown are verified on pinned `SONiC.internal.162324073-6068fbb477`. This is an older master-family baseline; the latest image was blocked by an unrelated platform-init BIOS sysfs read, so latest-image qualification is not claimed.

The full master suite is terminal and **did not pass**: pytest reported 50 passed, 3 failed, 7 skipped, 1 xfailed, 1 xpassed, and 53 teardown errors.

The three body failures are the SONiC relay source-interface Option-82 case, source-interface non-default VRF case, and different-VRF case.

#### Source-interface/Option-82 investigation

The two VRF body failures are known issues. The remaining default-VRF source-interface/Option-82 failure is an old-image/new-test mismatch: the saved capture contains all 48 forwarded DISCOVERs, but their link-selection address is `192.168.0.0` rather than the test's expected `192.168.0.1`. Offline replay with the original PTF matcher gives 0/48 matches originally and 48/48 when only that address is adjusted. The April image predates the existing sonic-dhcp-relay fix https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcp-relay/pull/121. No test code was changed and no separate stock-DHCPmon baseline comparison was run.

That independent relay fix, merged on 2026-07-22, replaced `VLAN address & subnet mask` with the receiving VLAN address for Link Selection SubOption 5. The captured packets show the earlier subnet-address encoding; the current test expects the later VLAN-address encoding. The offline replay is diagnostic evidence, not a new passing hardware test or a weakened assertion.

The 53 errors are log-analysis failures matching `syncd` SAI port-attribute messages, including RX signal-detect reads returning `Invalid port`. No separate baseline comparison was performed for those log-analysis failures; they are not all reclassified as confirmed pre-existing failures or dismissed. The raw master suite counts remain unchanged, and latest-image qualification is still not claimed.

Posttest passed (5 passed), no new DHCPmon core was found, the original master-image stock binary was restored byte-for-byte (SHA-256 `40505c0aab71b0efe73a7c958b100543f54061ce60c82f2cdcbb8386a1a9ad36`), and final services/Redis/12-BGP checks passed.

Thus the controlled-shutdown and startup-race evidence is positive on both branches, and the 202605 full regression passed, but the master full regression remains a qualification gap. Additional final-package synchronization and first-hop DHCPv6 health, genuine loss and recovery checks are now verified: https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcpmon/pull/122#issuecomment-6174921765. The nested-wrapper and older-image qualification limitations remain explicit there.

@Xichen96 - Recommendation: address the remaining startup shutdown race before approval. Reviewed head `26d08881dd682d2c77262297681ec535005fa18c`.

**[P2] Preserve fatal-stop requests across event-loop startup.**

[`sock_mgr_start_event_loop()`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcpmon/blob/26d08881dd682d2c77262297681ec535005fa18c/src/sock_mgr.cpp#L590-L601) launches workers before the [main loop enters dispatch](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcpmon/blob/26d08881dd682d2c77262297681ec535005fa18c/src/dhcp_mon.cpp#L785-L797). An early packet callback can throw and call [`dhcp_mon_stop_on_failure()`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcpmon/blob/26d08881dd682d2c77262297681ec535005fa18c/src/dhcp_mon.cpp#L829-L834) while the main loop or later workers have not entered dispatch yet. Libevent resets its break flag on entry to `event_base_loop()`, so those pre-dispatch `loopbreak` requests are lost.

The originating worker can exit while the main/later loops continue. If no subsequent callback throws, DHCPmon remains partially running instead of completing the intended nonzero failure shutdown.

I read the [existing response](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcpmon/pull/121#discussion_r4255181134) and agree that this is a narrow worker-startup window, not the normal periodic DB-update failure path. However, a later exception is not a guaranteed shutdown mechanism, and the planned removal of the worker Redis lookup is not part of this head. This is the already-discussed issue, not a separate new finding; closing the thread as out of scope leaves the behavior present.

Please make fatal-stop notification survive startup, using a startup-safe notification or synchronized pending-failure handoff. A deterministic regression case should hold the main/later worker loops before dispatch, trigger a fatal callback in an active worker, then release startup and require bounded completion, worker joins, and a nonzero result without another exception.

No additional blocking issue found in the main DB-exception shutdown path. This is a comment only, not a formal review-state change.

@StormLiangMS @ashutosh-agrawal The startup shutdown race is now fixed on master head `c5bc7543cd32be3c2b64cb0cc22fdf800b74e09e`.

Wow, Astra really was better for this one. I was aware of the race and had Sol working on it for a few hours without reaching an acceptable fix. After switching to Astra, we worked out this minimal fix pretty quickly.

Each existing fatal-stop path now requests:

```cpp
event_base_loopbreak(base);
event_base_loopexit(base, NULL);
```

`loopbreak()` retains immediate shutdown for an already-running loop. If a main or worker loop has not entered dispatch, Libevent clears the pre-dispatch break flag on entry, but the queued `loopexit()` callback survives and stops that late-starting loop. Shutdown no longer depends on another exception.

The callback detecting the failure is necessarily executing inside an active loop. That originating loop observes its break immediately after the callback returns, before processing its queued exit callback, so its `got_exit` remains false. The unchanged post-join success check requires `got_exit` from the main loop and every worker; therefore the process retains its nonzero failure result even when the other loops stop through the queued-exit fallback. The existing normal/fatal-overlap policy is unchanged.

The deterministic actual-binary check on the final-source 202605 package held the main and three later workers before dispatch and triggered one production packet callback exception in the active worker. The pre-fix binary hung; the fixed binary returned from all five loops, completed joins/cleanup, and exited with status 1 without a second exception. Normal SIGTERM shutdown separately exited with status 0. The fixture is validation-only and adds no production readiness synchronization, state, or callbacks.

Master amd64, arm64 and armhf CI is green. The same fix is in the combined manual 202605 backport, https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcpmon/pull/122, head `76ff4c8376fd97515bb579160e9cebb92fa13ddb`. The remaining full-suite validation and separate master runtime campaign are still in progress; the runtime check above is specifically 202605 evidence.

@vaibhavhd, could you approve the combined **202605 backport** in https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcpmon/pull/122?

We want to include these three fixes:

- **[Controlled shutdown—newly merged](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcpmon/pull/121):** On 202605, `tests/process_monitoring/test_critical_process_monitoring.py::test_monitoring_critical_processes` has been failing and producing DHCPmon core dumps when the test deliberately terminates Redis. - **[Counter-synchronization protection](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcpmon/pull/114):** We are seeing many false DHCPmon alarms on piloted devices. This prevents counter clearing/synchronization from triggering false disparity alerts through stale health snapshots.
- **[DHCPv6 health matching](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcpmon/pull/101):** This addresses false alarms on piloted devices caused by normal DHCPv6 relay transformations being incorrectly treated as missing transmissions.

The exact combined backport was tested on **SONiC.20260510.20**: full DHCP suite **48 passed / 11 skipped**, **16 exercised Redis-loss shutdowns without aborts or new cores**, and passing startup, counter-sync, and first-hop DHCPv6 health/loss/recovery checks. [Detailed evidence](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcpmon/pull/122#issuecomment-6174921765) records the remaining nested-relay coverage limitation.

@StormLiangMS Here is the design reasoning behind the current boundary.

We are working toward one long-running `dhcpmon` process that handles configuration refresh, multiple VLANs, and both IPv4 and IPv6. In that model, the daemon should consume the authoritative CONFIG_DB state and dynamically reconcile VLAN, family, upstream-interface, and Loopback0 changes.

Passing configured-family intent through supervisor command-line parameters would be a detour from that design. It would:

- create a second, startup-only source of configuration truth;
- require supervisor regeneration and process restart after configuration changes;
- reinforce the current process-per-VLAN model;
- require another redesign when multi-VLAN dynamic reconciliation moves into the daemon.

That is why https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-dhcpmon/pull/111 is intentionally limited to separating the IPv4 and IPv6 lifecycles. One unavailable family no longer prevents the other from starting, while the existing passive-monitoring behavior remains unchanged.

The planned sequence is:

1. This PR establishes independent IPv4/IPv6 capability.
2. https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/27277 consumes the propagated source and supplies the correct VLAN and upstream rendering, including IPv6-only operation.
3. The follow-up configuration-refresh work consolidates monitoring into one process and dynamically manages multiple VLANs, both families, and late address changes.

The late Dual-ToR Loopback0 case follows the same reasoning. Today, family availability is intentionally a startup snapshot and later address changes require restart. A one-off startup flag or retry path would not provide the dynamic reconciliation the final design needs.

I believe keeping this prerequisite focused and avoiding a temporary external-parameter interface is the cleaner design. However, this is a design tradeoff, and I will follow your final judgment if you prefer immediate configured-family gating despite the expected later rework.

## Code Review

### Critical

1. **`src/packet_handler.cpp` — `find_dhcpv6_option` / `dhcpv6_sanity_check`**: Off-by-one in DHCPv6 option parsing. The boundary check `while (offset + 1 < dhcp6_options_sz)` only ensures 2 bytes exist, but 4 bytes are immediately read (code at `offset`, len at `offset+2`). If only 2–3 bytes remain, `ntohs(*(uint16_t *)(dhcp6_options + offset + 2))` is an out-of-bounds read. Should be `offset + 4 <= dhcp6_options_sz`. Same pattern in `dhcpv6_sanity_check`.

2. **`src/packet_handler.cpp` — `ipv6_sanity_check`**: IPv6 extension header traversal bug. When the loop finds `nxt_hdr[0] == IPPROTO_UDP`, it advances the pointer *past* the UDP header with `nxt_hdr += (nxt_hdr[1] + 1) * 8` before returning. The returned pointer points to data *after* the actual UDP header. Should return `(struct udphdr *)nxt_hdr` immediately after confirming IPPROTO_UDP, without the extra advance.

3. **`src/dhcp_mon.cpp` — `db_counters_initialized`**: `mCountersDbPtr->hget(...)` returns `std::shared_ptr<std::string>`. The code assigns to `std::string *field = ... .get()` extracting the raw pointer, but the `shared_ptr` is destroyed at the semicolon, leaving `field` as a dangling pointer. The subsequent `field->empty()` is use-after-free. Store the `shared_ptr` in a local variable to keep it alive.

4. **`src/dhcp_device.cpp` — `dhcp_device_check_positive_health`**: Unsafe cast `(const int *)monitored_msgs` where `monitored_msgs` is `const dhcp_message_type_t[]` (enum). Underlying type of unscoped enums is implementation-defined. Should use a properly typed array or explicit conversion.

### High

5. **`src/sock_mgr.cpp` — `sock_mgr_start_event_loop`**: Thread lambda captures `info` by reference from a range-based for loop over `sock_map` (an `unordered_map`). If the map is rehashed, all references become dangling. Capture by value or look up by key.

6. **`src/dhcp_device.cpp` — `initialize_intf_mac_and_ip_addr`**: Requires exactly 1 IPv4, 1 IPv6 GUA, and 1 IPv6 LLA on every interface. This is overly strict — some interfaces (e.g. loopback) may legitimately lack an address type. Will cause init failures on valid configurations.

7. **`src/packet_handler.cpp` — `callback_common`**: `debug_mask` is set as thread-local but modified without RAII guard. If `packet_handler` throws, `debug_mask` is never restored. Use an RAII pattern.

### Medium

8. **`src/sock_mgr.cpp` — `sock_mgr_drain_sock_buffer`**: Stack buffer `char buf[65536]` is 64KB on the stack. Could cause stack overflow on constrained systems. Use heap allocation or existing sock_info buffers.

9. **`src/packet_handler.h` — `DHCPV6_OPTION_CODE_MAX = 150`**: Hardcoded limit is arbitrary. IANA assigns DHCPv6 option codes up to ~200+ and growing. This will reject legitimate packets with newer option codes. Should be set much higher or removed.

10. **`src/dhcp_check_profile.h`**: `std::unordered_map` with enum keys relies on implicit hash support from GCC, which isn't guaranteed by the standard. Consider `std::map` or defining a custom hash.

11. **`objects.mk`**: `-levent` appears twice in the LIBS line. Harmless but indicates sloppy dependency management.

---

Overall the architectural refactoring (pcap filters, modular `sock_mgr`/`packet_handler`/`health_check`/`dhcp_check_profile`) looks solid and the DHCPv6 protocol handling (relay-forward/reply, link-addr) is generally correct. **Items 1–3 are must-fix before merge** — they can cause crashes or memory corruption on crafted packets.

Thanks for the thorough review. Here's the status of each item:

Critical

1. Off-by-one in find_dhcpv6_option / dhcpv6_sanity_check Fixed in e73a9a2. Changed find_dhcpv6_option to offset + 3 < dhcp6_options_sz to ensure the full 4-byte option header is available. dhcpv6_sanity_check was already safe — it reads the 2-byte type code first, then has a secondary guard if (offset + 3 >= dhcp6_options_sz) before reading the length.
Added comments to both functions documenting the boundary checks at each step.

2. IPv6 extension header traversal in ipv6_sanity_check The code is correct. When the loop finds nxt_hdr[0] == IPPROTO_UDP, nxt_hdr points at the last extension header whose next-header field indicates UDP follows. The advance nxt_hdr += (nxt_hdr[1] + 1) * 8 skips past this extension header to reach the actual UDP header. Without this advance, we'd return
a pointer to the extension header, not the UDP header. Added a comment clarifying this in dece900.

3. Dangling pointer in db_counters_initialized Fixed in 7a7528f. Stored the shared_ptr in local variables instead of extracting the raw pointer via .get(). Also cleaned up an unnecessary .get() call at another hget site and added a comment explaining why shared_ptr keeps the string alive.

4. Unsafe enum cast (const int *)monitored_msgs Intentional. The helper functions (check_counter_not_transmitted, check_counter_increased, check_counters_delta_expected) use const int * to accept both dhcp_message_type_t and dhcpv6_message_type_t arrays without duplicating the function for each enum type. Safe on all SONiC platforms (GCC/Linux) where
unscoped enums use int as the underlying type. Added a comment in 09157c7.

High

5. Thread captures reference in sock_mgr_start_event_loop Safe in current code — sock_map is fully populated before sock_mgr_start_event_loop and never modified afterward. Added a comment warning that the map must not be modified after this point in e630b0e.

6. Overly strict initialize_intf_mac_and_ip_addr Intentional. dhcpmon requires IPv4, IPv6 GUA, and IPv6 LLA on each monitored interface for packet validation in the check profiles (src/dst IP matching). All interfaces passed to dhcpmon (-id, -iu, -im) are expected to have all address types in a properly configured SONiC DHCP relay setup. The loopback
interface call has its own separate handling.

7. debug_mask no RAII guard in callback_common Safe without RAII. The packet handlers (packet_handler, packet_handler_v6) are void functions with internal error handling — they do not throw. Even if debug_mask were stuck at false, the next loop iteration resets it. Added a comment in 54a3a61.

Medium

8. 64KB stack buffer in sock_mgr_drain_sock_buffer Acceptable. This is a drain function called once during init, not recursively. The default Linux stack size is 8MB. 64KB is well within limits for all SONiC platforms.
